overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of the blind spot argument. You'll be asked about the Blind Spot, the amnesia of experience, the parable of temperature, the target of the critique, and the book's reading of the hard problem.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: What do Frank, Gleiser, and Thompson mean by science's "Blind Spot"?

options.html: A set of phenomena that current instruments can't detect
options.text: A set of phenomena that current instruments can't detect
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The Blind Spot isn't missing data. It's science's failure to see the experience it depends on.

options.html: Science's failure to see the lived experience it depends on
options.text: Science's failure to see the lived experience it depends on
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Science depends on experience at every step, but its dominant self-image treats experience as secondary.

options.html: A bias that makes scientists reject evidence they dislike
options.text: A bias that makes scientists reject evidence they dislike
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The Blind Spot concerns experience as science's starting point, not motivated reasoning.

options.html: A region of the retina that science has failed to explain
options.text: A region of the retina that science has failed to explain
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The eye's blind spot is the book's guiding image, not its thesis.

forms.stemHtml: In the parable of temperature, where does the error the authors identify lie?

options.html: In early thermometers, which gave inaccurate readings
options.text: In early thermometers, which gave inaccurate readings
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The instruments are an achievement. The error lies in ranking the abstraction above experience.
Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors accept thermodynamics. The error is in how its results are interpreted.

options.html: In taking the abstract concept as more real than felt warmth
options.text: In taking the abstract concept as more real than felt warmth
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The authors call this an inversion: the abstraction is ranked above the experience it came from.

options.html: In trusting felt warmth over measurements
options.text: In trusting felt warmth over measurements
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The parable doesn't favor felt warmth over measurement. It criticizes forgetting where measurement comes from.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following belong to the target of the authors' critique? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The idea that physical reality is all there is
options.text: The idea that physical reality is all there is
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Physicalism is one component of the worldview the authors criticize.

options.html: The idea that science gives a God's-eye view of nature
options.text: The idea that science gives a God's-eye view of nature
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The authors reject the image of science as describing reality from no standpoint.

options.html: Treating scientific abstractions as more real than experience
options.text: Treating scientific abstractions as more real than experience
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is the core of what the book calls Blind Spot metaphysics.

options.html: The experimental method of the natural sciences
options.text: The experimental method of the natural sciences
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors target a worldview attached to science, not scientific method.
Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors accept thermodynamics. They criticize ranking it above felt warmth.

forms.stemHtml: What do Frank, Gleiser, and Thompson call the forgetting of the lived experience from which scientific concepts arise, so that abstract structures are taken for the whole of reality? Enter three words.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It's the forgetting that lets an abstraction be taken for reality.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors call it the amnesia of experience.

forms.stemHtml: How does The Blind Spot read the hard problem of consciousness?

options.html: As a puzzle that neuroscience is close to solving
options.text: As a puzzle that neuroscience is close to solving
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors don't treat it as a puzzle to solve within the current framework.

options.html: As proof that consciousness is an illusion
options.text: As proof that consciousness is an illusion
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The authors treat experience as the starting point, not an illusion.

options.html: As a problem only for dualists
options.text: As a problem only for dualists
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. On their reading, the problem arises from physicalist metaphysics.

options.html: As a symptom of the blind spot
options.text: As a symptom of the blind spot
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Experience is abstracted away to build physical concepts, and then it looks like something extra to fit back in.

title: The Blind Spot Argument
